new_findings.requirement: Eval quality: a case's graded expectation must be established by the bytes the worker can actually see.
affected_sections: cases.jsonl DX-B-011 expectations.summary and assertion A1 expect
evidence: The new case states that "PROD-001@2 REQ-004 accepts an account only for served postcodes and requires an immediate out-of-area rejection" and grades on whether "the contradiction with REQ-004 is named".

The bytes the worker sees say only: "REQ-004 | A new neighbour can create an account with an email address and a postcode, and is told immediately when the postcode is outside the served area. | The served-area list is fixed and known at signup time." (fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md line 32). That mandates immediate notification; it does not state that account creation is refused.

The rejection reading is established elsewhere - fixtures/stale/PROD-001.md line 36 records revision 3 changing REQ-004 and notes "Immediate rejection is no longer the accepted behaviour" - but DX-B-011 sets files to [fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md] and candidate_subpath to shared, so the worker cannot see that fixture.

Consequence: a worker that reads revision 2 carefully and concludes REQ-004 does not settle whether an out-of-area account may exist, then routes the request as an uncovered product-scope question rather than as a contradiction, is behaving correctly and would still miss the case's stated expectation.
new_findings.impact: Narrow. The behaviour the case exists to discriminate - record and route to the owning artifact, versus draw it as though the requirement permitted it - is exercised under either reading, and a reviewer applying the rubric has the latitude to judge it. But the graded wording rests on an interpretation the worker cannot reach from its own inputs, which is the same class of mistake the skill itself warns about under "Inventing the requirement".
new_findings.uncertainty: The fixture set's own authoring clearly intends the rejection reading; this is a wording gap in the case, not a wrong premise.
new_findings.recommendation: Widen the expectation to accept either reading while still requiring the routing behaviour - for example: named as contradicting REQ-004, or as a scope question REQ-004 does not settle, and in either case recorded as a change request against PROD-001 with the affected rows identified rather than drawn as though the requirement permitted it. Change only cases.jsonl DX-B-011 and evals.json id 11.
new_findings.explicitly_do_not: Do not edit fixtures/shared/PROD-001.md to make REQ-004 say 'rejected'. Its bytes are byte-identical to fixtures/stale/preserved/PROD-001.r2.md (both b863996bf1804f08980e5f051e9f568fa5e3187c1a70faa3f45f6e3e0f43e8f9), which is the sentinel DX-B-008 A2 hard-codes; editing it would break that case and destroy the preserved-revision relationship DX-B-008 exists to test.

new_findings.requirement: trigger-queries.json split_policy: "Fixed and stratified by should_trigger and category"
evidence: Moving A7b to the new negative_change category left two categories single-sided, not one. Recomputed composition: negative_change holds one entry on the validation side and none on train; negative_define_product now holds one entry on train (A7a) and none on validation. Before the re-cut every one of the eight categories had at least one entry on each side.

The revision_note discloses only the first half: "negative_change now holds one entry, on the validation side, so it contributes no train-side signal - an owner allocating tier A may want a second query in it first." It does not mention that negative_define_product lost its validation entry in the same move.
split_policy still reads "Fixed and stratified by should_trigger and category" without qualification, which is now true of six categories rather than eight.
new_findings.impact: No expected value is wrong and no measurement is invalidated - tier A has never been run. The effect is on a future tier-A allocation: a per-category train-versus-validation report is impossible for two categories rather than the one the file admits to, so an owner reading the disclosure would under-count the work needed to rebalance.
new_findings.uncertainty: None. The author disclosed the re-cut and one of its two consequences deliberately and honestly; this is an incomplete disclosure, not a concealed one.
new_findings.recommendation: Extend the revision_note's known-limit sentence to name both categories, and qualify split_policy's stratification claim to match. Alternatively add one query to each of negative_change (train) and negative_define_product (validation) and restore full stratification. Either is a single-file edit.
